comparison.objective: Candidate adjusts and locks a robot-gripper opening stop at 90° and verifies retained motion; pr-360 caps four color-matched pens and sorts them into marked areas.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate tests concentric driver-and-wrench seating, coupled screw/jam-nut countertorque, setting preservation, tool withdrawal, and articulated cycling. pr-360 tests cap-to-barrel alignment/insertion, repeated object handling, color matching, and planar sorting.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires locked angle accuracy, limited stop drift through three cycles, retained nuts, and released clearance. pr-360 requires all four matching caps retained and each released pen resting within its color area; its versions specify numeric insertion, rest, containment, and clearance criteria, with no material rubric detail missing for this comparison.
comparison.reason: They share only generic bimanual handling, retention, and hands-clear checks; pr-360 does not test rotational counterholding that preserves an adjustable setting against locknut reaction or subsequent functional-cycle retention, while the candidate does not test repeated cap insertion or color sorting.
